turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Mrs Keller, obs are done. Blood pressure's one-eighteen over seventy-four, pulse ninety-six beats a minute, temperature thirty-seven point two Celsius, oxygen sats ninety-eight percent on air. He won't be a minute.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, well I've been rotting in that chair. I feel shocking and I just want to go home.
[SEG0003] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Parking was hopeless, three laps of the block. She's worn out, that's all. Sorry we're a bit frazzled.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm not worn out, I'm cranky and tired. Stop narrating me. Can we just get in?
[SEG0005] person_4 (DOCTOR): In you come. What's happened?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Spewing, and the runs. After my niece's wedding.
[SEG0007] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Saturday, down in Geelong. Big sit-down, prawns and then chicken. I went along with her.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): I can talk, thanks. Sunday morning it hit, both ends. Today's Tuesday, so that's two days. Happy days.
[SEG0009] person_4 (DOCTOR): Vomiting and diarrhoea, both?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Both. Brought up, um, four times Sunday... well actually I think it was three, I lost the plot. Less yesterday. If I skull the water it comes straight back.
[SEG0011] person_4 (DOCTOR): How many bowel motions today?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Six. Or seven. I stopped counting after lunch, so more than that maybe. It's just water, no form to it.
[SEG0013] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any blood?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No blood.
[SEG0015] person_4 (DOCTOR): Pain in the tummy?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Crampy, low down, since it started. Comes in waves. Worse just before I hit the loo.
[SEG0017] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She was up half the night with it. The wedding band was pretty average too, trumpet miles out. Not that you asked.
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Nobody cares about the trumpet. Yes, the cramps, low down. Can we move on?
[SEG0019] person_4 (DOCTOR): Managing a drink?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Sips only. Food, nah. The coffee smell in the corridor nearly set me off again.
[SEG0021] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Barely a cup all day. Her mouth's dry, and she only passed urine once, this morning. It was dark.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Once. Dark. I was going to say it.
[SEG0023] person_4 (DOCTOR): Fever?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Sunday night I felt hot. Not today. I haven't been shaky or anything.
[SEG0025] person_4 (DOCTOR): Others from the wedding unwell?
[SEG0026] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Sister Karen, and two of the cousins, same bug. Karen's still taking her biotin, those hair tablets from the chemist, but that's hers. Margaret doesn't touch them.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Good, because I don't want Karen's vitamins. She's always flogging some bottle.
[SEG0028] person_4 (DOCTOR): Taken anything for the diarrhoea?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Loperamide. Chemist Imodium, two milligrams. Two tablets yesterday arvo, and today three... or is it four? I honestly can't remember.
[SEG0030] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Don't leave that bit out. The nurse on the phone told her not to take a stopper while she's vomiting. I passed that on. She took them anyway.
[SEG0031] person_4 (DOCTOR): Stop the loperamide. It'll hold the bug in. Regular medicines?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Perindopril four milligrams every morning, for my high blood pressure, years now. Panadol sometimes for sore knees, five hundred milligrams, two tablets.
[SEG0033] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She left the perindopril out this morning. Didn't want to heave it straight back up.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): One dose, this morning, that's all. And no Panadol since before the wedding. Knees can wait.
[SEG0035] person_4 (DOCTOR): Open your mouth for me.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Your hands are freezing, just so you know. The air con in here is ridiculous.
[SEG0037] person_4 (DOCTOR): Tongue's dry. Abdomen's soft, tender across the lower part, no guarding. Skin turgor on the hand is a touch slow. Mild dehydration, nothing dramatic.
[SEG0038] person_1 (NURSE): Sorry to butt in. Repeat pulse is still ninety-six, and there's a jug of water at the desk if you want it. I'll leave you to it.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't want a jug. I want a bed.
[SEG0040] person_4 (DOCTOR): This is a gastro, most likely from that wedding meal, with the others crook too. Working impression only. A bacterial one is possible, I can't rule it out sitting here.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Fantastic. So I just suffer, do I?
[SEG0042] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Does she need a test? Also the blue bag's in the car if you need the Medicare card, under the seat I think. Sorry, not helpful.
[SEG0043] person_4 (DOCTOR): No sample today. If the diarrhoea hasn't settled in a couple of days, or if you see blood, we'll send a stool sample.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): A couple more days of this. Lovely.

[SEG0045] person_4 (DOCTOR): Treatment is fluid. Small sips of Gastrolyte, often, or diluted juice if that tastes better, and no big gulps. Leave the loperamide alone. Start the perindopril for your blood pressure again once the sips stay down.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Gastrolyte tastes like the ocean. I'll try. I'm not promising I'll enjoy it.
[SEG0047] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Should she pinch some of Karen's biotin as well, for energy? There's a bottle at Karen's place.
[SEG0048] person_4 (DOCTOR): No. Biotin is your sister's, and it does nothing for a gastro. Don't take other people's tablets.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Wasn't planning to. Can I lie down at home or not?
[SEG0050] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes. If you can't keep fluid down, you get dizzy, the urine dries up, or there's blood, come back sooner. If you're not better in two days, come back and see me.
[SEG0051] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Righto. I'll get her home and keep the sips going. Thanks for fitting us in.
